info.description:
REST API for practicing QA automation and API testing.

**Base URL:** /api/v1

**Authentication:**
- Create a user with POST /users/create to receive an access_token
- Or use POST /login with existing credentials to get a new access_token
- Include the token in Authorization header as: Bearer {your_access_token}
- Token required for: PUT, PATCH, DELETE operations

**Auto-Deletion:**
- All users are automatically deleted after 24 hours (TTL)
- Maximum 1,000,000 users allowed in database

**Rate Limiting:**
- User creation: 100 requests per minute per IP
- General API: 10 requests per second

**Quick Start:**
1. POST /users/create with email, username, password, profile.first_name, profile.last_name
2. Save the access_token from response
3. Use the token for authenticated operations (PUT, PATCH, DELETE)
info.title: User API

get.description: Counts computed in ONE aggregation, so the three numbers are a single snapshot of a collection that a 24h TTL index is deleting from underneath. `by_role` always carries every role key, zero-filled — an absent key would be indistinguishable from a serialisation bug. Documents written before `metadata.role` existed are counted as `user`, which is the truth about their effective permissions.

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

403.description: Valid token, but the account is not an admin

get.description: The ordinary user list plus `has_active_token` per row — whether that account is currently logged in. Accepts the same page/per_page/sort/filter/search contract as GET /users/list, validated by the same code. NOTE what it does not add: `metadata.last_login_ip` stays owner-only even here. An admin token is not a way around it, because the seed code that mints an admin is published — if admins could read it, closing the leak would mean nothing.
get.summary: List users with the operator fields (admin)

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

403.description: Valid token, but the account is not an admin

delete.description: Scoped to your own account on this practice server, for the same reason SetRole is: the seed code is published, so an unscoped delete would let any visitor remove other students' accounts and the sandbox users the challenge system verifies against. Deleting yourself also invalidates your token, so the next admin call answers 401 — a clean demonstration that 401 and 403 are different failures.

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

403.description: Not an admin, or the target is not your own account

patch.description: Privilege management. Allowed values are `user` and `admin`; the data model's enum also contains `moderator`, but v1 refuses to grant it — that difference is deliberate, not an oversight. On this practice server the target must be your OWN account: admins are obtainable by anyone with the published seed code, so cross-user mutation would let one student rewrite another's. Demoting yourself from admin to user is the intended exercise, and it is irreversible without a new seed call.

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

403.description: Not an admin, or the target is not your own account

get.description: The authenticated player's reports, newest first. `total` (all reports of the player) and `reports` come from one snapshot, `returned` = len(reports). No PII.

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

post.description: Deterministic scoring of a bug report about one of the catalog bugs — five criteria (has_steps 25, steps_reproducible 20, expected_actual 25, severity_reasonable 15, title_quality 15), each with an `ok`/`fail` feedback item and the parameters that explain the rule. Bearer is OPTIONAL: with a valid token the report is stored for 24h (201, `saved:true`, `report_id`), without a header it is only scored (200, `saved:false`, nothing stored). A presented but invalid/expired token is a 401, never a silent anonymous submit.

parameters.description: The report (steps 1..20 non-blank lines, severity low|medium|high|critical)
parameters.name: request

401.description: Authorization header present but the token is invalid or expired

404.description: bug_id is not in the catalog

429.description: On average 30 reports per minute per IP (burst 10)

get.description: Full report of the authenticated owner (steps, expected, actual, score with feedback). A foreign, unknown or malformed id is the same 404 — nothing about other players is revealed.

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

get.description: The three intentionally buggy endpoints: id, method, path and the i18n keys of title, description and EXPECTED behaviour (the frontend shows the expectation behind a spoiler). No severity metadata — that would spoil the bug-report scoring.

post.description: **This endpoint contains an intentional logic bug** (practice): the returned `total` is not sum(price × qty). Prices are parsed as exact decimals (at most two fraction digits) and summed in integer cents, so rounding is NOT the defect. Send two or more positions and check the arithmetic.

parameters.description: Cart positions (1..50); price is a bare decimal number, qty 1..1000
parameters.name: request

200.description: The total as the server computes it

400.description: Body is not JSON, items empty, price not a 2-decimal number, qty out of range

get.description: **This endpoint contains an intentional logic bug** (practice): status 200 does not mean the value is right. A 25-item deterministic dataset paginated by `page`/`per_page` — compare the number of returned items with `per_page` on a full page and with `total`. Which pages reproduce the problem?

200.description: One page — count the items yourself

400.description: page / per_page out of range or not a number

get.description: **This endpoint contains an intentional logic bug** (practice): the event starts at 09:00 LOCAL time of the requested IANA zone, but the returned instant is shifted. `tz` is required — in UTC the defect is invisible. Try a zone with a DST transition on that date.

Public static catalog of server-verified challenges. `title`/`description` are i18n keys resolved by the frontend; `params` is the schema of the verify body (empty for the starter challenges). Progress is not mixed in — see GET /challenges/progress.

Solved challenges of the authenticated player in catalog order, with points. Progress is keyed by the player (user id), so it survives login token rotation; it expires together with the user (24h TTL). No PII.

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

get.description: Public: how many hints a challenge has and their kinds (1 nudge, 2 approach, 3 solution). Never carries the hint keys/texts — those come only from POST /challenges/{id}/hints/reveal (which records the reveal) and from GET /challenges/progress (already revealed).

post.description: Reveals hints strictly in order. The body names the level you want: an already revealed level (idempotent repeat — same answer, nothing recorded) or exactly the next one (recorded). Asking for a level above the next one is refused with 409 — nothing is skipped, and a retried request can never reveal more than you asked for. The answer always carries every revealed level (`revealed`) so one response restores the state. Revealing does not require an open attempt; the level revealed at the moment of a solve is snapshotted into progress as `hints_used`.

parameters.description: Level to reveal (1..3): the next one or an already revealed one
parameters.name: request

400.description: Body is not JSON or level is missing / not an integer 1..3

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

409.description: Level above the next one — reveal the previous levels first

post.description: Creates a server-owned sandbox user for the player and records the baseline the verifier will compare against. 201 = fresh attempt with the sandbox credentials (email, username, password, access_token). 200 = the existing open attempt (credentials without the token — log in to get one; `target_missing:true` when the sandbox no longer exists, use `?reset=true`), or `already_solved:true` when the challenge is solved (nothing is created — one solve per player and challenge). `reset=true` abandons the open attempt, deletes its sandbox and issues a new one. Same rate budget as POST /users/create.

parameters.description: Abandon the open attempt and start a fresh one
parameters.name: reset

200.description: Existing open attempt, or already solved

400.description: reset must be true or false

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

409.description: No open attempt could be issued (concurrent reset) — start again

post.description: Checks that the attempt's sandbox moved from its baseline to the goal state. 200 for both outcomes: `solved:true` (with `points_awarded`, or `already_solved:true` and 0 points on a repeat) or `solved:false` with a `detail` explaining what is still missing. Body is optional: `attempt_id` pins an attempt (otherwise the open one is used); `params` must match the challenge's declared schema (empty for the starter challenges — any key is rejected). Repeated and concurrent verifies are idempotent and return the original `solved_at`.

400.description: Body is not JSON, params is null/not an object, unknown or missing param

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or expired token

409.description: No open attempt — start the challenge first (never started, expired, reset, or foreign attempt_id)

get.description: Always returns Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, a strong ETag header ("chaos-v1", quoted on the wire; the JSON body carries the bare value chaos-v1) and a fixed Last-Modified — including on 304. If-None-Match takes precedence over If-Modified-Since (RFC 7232) and is compared weakly: W/"chaos-v1", a comma-separated list containing it, or * all yield 304 Not Modified without a body. If-Modified-Since is only consulted when If-None-Match is absent.

Waits N seconds (float, 0-9) and then returns 200. Values above 9 are clamped to 9 (clamped:true). Negative, non-numeric, NaN or Inf values are rejected with 400 INVALID_DELAY. Use it to practice client timeouts.
get.summary: Delay the response by N seconds

parameters.description: Seconds to wait (0-9; larger values are clamped)
parameters.name: seconds

400.description: INVALID_DELAY - negative, non-numeric, NaN or Inf

get.description: Reflects method, path, headers, query and body. Sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, X-Api-Key, X-Auth-Token) are masked as "***". Body is read up to 1 MiB (413 above); at most the first 64 KiB are reflected (truncated:true above, body:null). The body is reflected as text only for textual Content-Types (text/*, application/json, application/*+json, application/xml, application/*+xml, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, or no Content-Type) AND valid UTF-8; everything else (application/pdf, application/zip, image/*, …) is returned as body_base64 with encoding:"base64".

post.description: Reflects method, path, headers, query and body. Sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, X-Api-Key, X-Auth-Token) are masked as "***". Body is read up to 1 MiB (413 above); at most the first 64 KiB are reflected (truncated:true above, body:null). The body is reflected as text only for textual Content-Types (text/*, application/json, application/*+json, application/xml, application/*+xml, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, or no Content-Type) AND valid UTF-8; everything else (application/pdf, application/zip, image/*, …) is returned as body_base64 with encoding:"base64".

get.description: Fails with probability fail_rate (0.0-1.0, default 0.5) returning fail_status (400-599, default 500); otherwise returns 200. Without seed the roll comes from math/rand (not reproducible). With seed (any int64, decimal string) the roll is deterministic: the same seed + fail_rate ALWAYS yields the same outcome and the same roll — repeating a seeded request never turns a failure into a success, so use /chaos/flaky/sequence + /chaos/flaky/step/{index} for retry exercises. Headers: X-Chaos-Seed (the seed or "random"), X-Chaos-Roll (roll rounded to 4 decimals — display value; the exact float64 is in the body), X-Chaos-Deterministic (true/false). The body echoes seed as a JSON string (int64 is not JSON-number safe) and roll at full precision. NOTE: fail_status is dynamic — a failed roll with fail_status=400/429/503 returns that status with THIS body, while the same statuses from validation, the rate limiter or the proxy carry an ErrorResponse envelope (success:false) or a non-JSON body.
get.summary: Fail randomly — or reproducibly with a seed

parameters.description: int64 as a decimal string; makes the roll reproducible
parameters.name: seed

X-Chaos-Deterministic.description: true when a seed was supplied

X-Chaos-Roll.description: Roll in [0,1) rounded to 4 decimals (display value)

400.description: INVALID_SEED, INVALID_FAIL_RATE or INVALID_FAIL_STATUS (validation envelope). COLLISION: fail_status=400 on a failed roll returns 400 with a ChaosFlakyResponse body

418.description: Example of a custom fail_status (418 is never produced by infrastructure)

X-Chaos-Deterministic.description: true when a seed was supplied

X-Chaos-Roll.description: Roll in [0,1) rounded to 4 decimals (display value)

500.description: Roll failed (status is fail_status, 500 by default)

X-Chaos-Deterministic.description: true when a seed was supplied

X-Chaos-Roll.description: Roll in [0,1) rounded to 4 decimals (display value)

get.description: Returns the plan of the first `count` (1-50, default 10) indexed attempts for a seed: which of /chaos/flaky/step/0..count-1 fail. Step i uses roll = RollFromSeed(seed XOR i), failed = roll < fail_rate, status = failed ? fail_status : 200. steps[0] shares its roll with GET /chaos/flaky?seed=<seed> (same fail_rate). This is an INDEXED retry exercise: attempt i is a request to /chaos/flaky/step/i — repeating one unchanged URL never changes the outcome. first_success_index is an index; the number of attempts until success is first_success_index + 1 (-1 when every step fails). Pace recommendation: the global rate limit (10 req/s, burst 20, shared per IP) applies — for a client without concurrent traffic, >= 100 ms between attempts usually fits; a 429 (Go limiter) or 503 (proxy) is an infrastructure outcome outside the sequence: retry the SAME index after a pause.

parameters.description: Number of steps in the plan (1-50)
parameters.name: count

400.description: SEED_REQUIRED, INVALID_SEED, INVALID_COUNT, INVALID_FAIL_RATE or INVALID_FAIL_STATUS

429.description: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED — infrastructure outcome, not part of the plan

get.description: Responds with the REAL status of step `index` (0-49) of the seeded sequence — 200 when the step succeeds, fail_status when it fails — so a loop over /chaos/flaky/step/0, /1, /2 … is a genuine retry exercise (attempt i = request to /step/i; repeating one URL never changes its outcome). The body is always ChaosFlakyStepResponse and equals steps[index] of /chaos/flaky/sequence with the same seed/fail_rate/fail_status. fail_status is dynamic (400-599): with fail_status=400/429/503 a failed step returns that status with THIS body, whereas the same statuses from validation (400), the Go rate limiter (429) or the production proxy (503) carry an ErrorResponse envelope (success:false) or a non-JSON body — check for the envelope to tell them apart. Pace: >= 100 ms between attempts is a recommendation for a client without concurrent traffic (global limit 10 req/s, burst 20 per IP); on 429/503 retry the SAME index after a pause.
get.summary: One indexed attempt of the seeded sequence

parameters.description: Status returned when the step fails (400-599)
parameters.name: fail_status

X-Chaos-Roll.description: Roll rounded to 4 decimals (display value; exact value in the body)

400.description: INVALID_INDEX, SEED_REQUIRED, INVALID_SEED, INVALID_FAIL_RATE or INVALID_FAIL_STATUS (validation envelope). COLLISION: a failed step with fail_status=400 returns 400 with a ChaosFlakyStepResponse body — tell them apart by success:false / error.code, present only in the envelope

418.description: Example of a custom fail_status (418 is never produced by infrastructure)

X-Chaos-Roll.description: Roll rounded to 4 decimals (display value; exact value in the body)

429.description: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED from the Go limiter (infrastructure outcome, not part of the sequence). COLLISION: a failed step with fail_status=429 returns 429 with a ChaosFlakyStepResponse body

500.description: Step failed — the actual status equals fail_status; body is always ChaosFlakyStepResponse

X-Chaos-Roll.description: Roll rounded to 4 decimals (display value; exact value in the body)

503.description: nginx limit_req rejection in production (non-JSON, infrastructure outcome). COLLISION: a failed step with fail_status=503 returns 503 with a ChaosFlakyStepResponse body

get.description: Returns Content-Encoding: gzip regardless of Accept-Encoding. Use it to verify that your client decodes gzip transparently. Disable automatic decompression in your client (e.g. Go http.Transport{DisableCompression:true}) to see the raw compressed bytes.
get.summary: Always return a gzip-compressed JSON body

The optional type (301, 302, 307, 308; default 302) is propagated through every hop. 307/308 require clients to preserve method and body; 301/302 behaviour is client-specific. The optional type (301, 302, 307, 308; default 302) is propagated through every hop. 307/308 require clients to preserve method and body; 301/302 behaviour is client-specific. get.description: Responds with the requested status code (200-599). Body is {"status_code", "message"} where message is Go's http.StatusText (empty string for non-standard codes such as 599). No body is written for 204, 205 and 304. Use it to exercise client retry logic, error handling and boundary tests.
get.summary: Return an arbitrary HTTP status code

200.description: Any 2xx-5xx code except 204/205/304 carries this body

400.description: INVALID_STATUS_CODE - code outside 200-599 or not an integer

get.description: Keeps the connection open for `after` seconds (default 8, max 60; larger values are clamped) and then returns 504 GATEWAY_TIMEOUT. Use it to practice client read timeouts: set your client timeout below `after` to see it fire. Values near 60 may hit the Cloudflare edge timeout in production.

400.description: INVALID_TIMEOUT - negative, non-numeric, NaN or Inf

504.description: GATEWAY_TIMEOUT - simulated upstream timeout after the hold

get.description: The files uploaded with THIS token, newest first. There is no public listing of every upload on purpose: the id is a capability, and an enumerable index would turn the sandbox into a file host. Anonymous uploads appear in nobody's list.

401.description: MISSING_TOKEN or INVALID_TOKEN

post.description:
Stores a file for 24 hours and returns its metadata. The media type in `content_type` is **detected from the content** (first 512 bytes); `declared_type` only echoes what the client claimed and never influences the decision.

Validation, in this exact order: a body larger than 5 MiB + 64 KiB is `413`; a body that is not parseable multipart is `400 INVALID_MULTIPART`; a missing `file` field is `400 NO_FILE`; a part over 5 MiB is `413`; an empty part is `400 EMPTY_FILE`; a description over 200 characters is `400`; an extension outside `.png .jpg .jpeg .pdf .txt .csv .json` is `415`; a supported extension whose content sniffs as something else is `422 CORRUPTED_FILE`; an exhausted payload budget is `503`.

Note that `.csv` and `.json` are detected as `text/plain` — content sniffing cannot tell them apart from a text file, and that limitation is part of the exercise.

The Bearer token is **optional**: without it the upload is anonymous (reachable only by its id, never listed); with it the file also appears in `GET /files`. A token that is present but invalid is a `401`, never a silent anonymous upload.

parameters.example: a screenshot for the bug report
parameters.description: Free-text note stored with the file
parameters.name: description

401.description: a token was presented but is invalid or expired

get.description: Metadata only, no content. Public: the id is the capability. The owner is never disclosed.

delete.description: Removes the file and frees its share of the payload budget. An anonymous file can be deleted by anyone holding its id (the id is the capability); a file uploaded with a token can only be deleted by that owner — for anybody else the answer is the same `404` as for a file that does not exist.

401.description: a token was presented but is invalid or expired

get.description:
Returns the raw bytes with an exact `Content-Length` and both `Content-Disposition` parameters: the ASCII `filename=` every client understands and the RFC 5987 `filename*` form that carries the real Unicode name percent-encoded.

`?inline=true` switches the disposition to `inline` (the browser renders it instead of saving); `?inline=false` is the default `attachment`. Any other value is a `400`.

The response always carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` — the API location does not inherit the site-wide security headers, so the handler sets them itself.
Returns basic health status of the API service. Use this endpoint to verify that the API is running and responding to requests.

post.description:
Splits a token and decodes its header and payload, the way a browser inspector does. Public and unauthenticated: it reads expired, forged and foreign tokens on purpose, because seeing what is inside a bad token is how you learn to debug one.

`signature_valid` has three possible answers. `true` means this server signed it, `false` means it did not, and `null` means the question cannot be answered because no signing secret is configured here. An expired but genuine token reports `true`: ageing out and being forged are different failures.

`expired` is `null` when the token carries no `exp` claim at all, which is neither expired nor valid forever as far as this endpoint is concerned.

Only unpadded base64url is accepted, as RFC 7515 requires. A padded segment is reported as a format error rather than silently decoded.
post.summary: Inspect any JWT without verifying it

post.description:
Exchanges credentials for two signed tokens. This is the **second, parallel** authentication scheme of the API: the opaque `usr_..._...` token issued by `POST /login` is NOT accepted here, and these JWTs are NOT accepted by the opaque endpoints.

The access token is short-lived (15 minutes by default) and the refresh token lives 24 hours. Both are signed with HS256 and carry `sub`, `email`, `type`, `jti`, `iat`, `exp` and `iss` — decode them at `POST /jwt/decode` to see for yourself.

Send `access_ttl_seconds` to get a deliberately short-lived access token (1 to 900 seconds). That is the intended way to practise the expired-token scenario without waiting fifteen minutes. It never affects the refresh token.

An unknown email and a wrong password give the same `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, so this endpoint cannot be used to discover which addresses exist.

This login does NOT rotate your opaque token: your existing session on the other pages of the platform keeps working.
post.summary: Get a JWT access and refresh token pair

401.description: INVALID_CREDENTIALS

get.description:
The protected endpoint of the JWT scheme. Requires an **access** token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; a refresh token is refused with `401 WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE`.

Every reason for refusal has its own code, which is the point of the exercise: `MISSING_TOKEN` (no header), `INVALID_TOKEN_FORMAT` (not three base64url segments), `INVALID_SIGNATURE` (signed with another secret, another algorithm, or not signed at all), `TOKEN_EXPIRED` (genuine signature, `exp` in the past), `INVALID_TOKEN` (a required claim is missing or wrong) and `WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE`.

Note that a token which is BOTH forged and expired reports `INVALID_SIGNATURE`: the signature is verified before any claim is read.

The user is not looked up in the database. A token stays valid until it expires even if the account is gone, which is the honest trade-off of stateless authentication.
get.summary: Read the claims of your access token

401.description: MISSING_TOKEN, INVALID_TOKEN_FORMAT, INVALID_SIGNATURE, TOKEN_EXPIRED, INVALID_TOKEN or WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE

post.description:
Validates the refresh token and issues a new access token with the server default lifetime, even if the original login asked for a short-lived one.

Checks happen in this order: format, signature, expiry, then token type. Sending an **access** token here is `401 WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE` — its signature is perfectly valid, it is simply the wrong kind of token, and telling those two situations apart is the exercise.

No new refresh token is returned and the old one keeps working until it expires. This is a refresh flow, not refresh rotation: real rotation needs server-side state to detect reuse, and its absence is the well-known cost of stateless tokens.
post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new access token

401.description: INVALID_TOKEN_FORMAT, INVALID_SIGNATURE, TOKEN_EXPIRED, INVALID_TOKEN or WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE

post.description: Authenticates user with email and password, returns a new access_token. The old token is invalidated immediately. Use this endpoint to refresh expired tokens or re-authenticate users. The new token must be used for all subsequent authenticated operations (PUT, PATCH, DELETE). Password comparison is currently plain-text (production should use bcrypt). Token format: usr_{timestamp}_{random32chars}.

400.description: Validation error - invalid email format or missing fields

401.description: Invalid credentials - wrong email or password

post.description: Creates a new temporary mailbox. Returns a token used to access the mailbox. The mailbox is automatically deleted after 15 minutes (TTL). Optionally specify a domain from the allowed list: play-qa.com, mail.play-qa.com, temp.play-qa.com, inbox.play-qa.com. Optionally provide a custom local_part (3-30 chars, a-z 0-9 _ -). Default domain is play-qa.com.

201.description: Mailbox created successfully with access token

400.description: Invalid domain or invalid local part

409.description: Address already taken, or local part is reserved for the SMTP Response Simulator

get.description: Retrieves mailbox information by token. Returns email address, domain, creation time, and expiration time.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a mailbox and all its messages. This operation cannot be undone. Returns 204 No Content on success.

get.description: Retrieves all messages for a mailbox identified by its token. Messages are sorted by received time (newest first). Body preview is truncated to 100 characters.
get.summary: List all messages in a mailbox

get.description: Retrieves a single message by its ID. The message must belong to the mailbox identified by the token. Returns full message data including HTML body.

post.description: Injects a test email message into the mailbox for practice purposes. Requires from, subject, and body fields. HTML body is optional. This endpoint simulates receiving an email and is useful for testing email-related automation scenarios.
post.summary: Inject a test message into a mailbox

post.description: Simulates sending an email to a recipient address. If the `to` address matches one of the predefined "magic" addresses (e.g. mailbox-full@play-qa.com, user-unknown@play-qa.com, rate-limited@play-qa.com), the server returns a stable, canned SMTP delivery response (accepted=false) so QA engineers can practice handling delivery failures — mailbox full (552), user unknown (550), rate limits (451), greylisting, policy rejections, TLS errors, and more. Magic addresses are matched on the local part only, so any allowed domain works. For any other recipient, the message is accepted (accepted=true) and stored in the mailbox. The local part of the address is matched case-insensitively. See the full list of magic addresses on the Temp Mail page.
post.summary: Send a message to a recipient (SMTP response simulator)

parameters.description: Recipient address and optional message fields
parameters.name: request

200.description: Simulated SMTP response (accepted=false for magic addresses, accepted=true otherwise)

get.description: The swagger.json file generated by swag init, served without runtime substitutions (host/schemes are not injected). It describes the same operations and schemas Swagger UI shows; /swagger/doc.json is a template render and may differ byte-wise. Stable URL for CI: curl -fsSLO -J https://play-qa.com/api/v1/openapi.json. Pass ?download=false to view inline.

The swagger.yaml file generated by swag init, served without runtime substitutions. Same operations and schemas as Swagger UI; import it into Postman, Insomnia or Bruno, or fetch it from CI. Pass ?download=false to view inline.

Generated at build time from the OpenAPI spec (openapi-to-postmanv2 + scripts/postman/augment.mjs). One folder per tag in teaching order, each split into a positive subfolder (one request per operation) and a negative subfolder (requests that reproduce every documented error, with pm.test on status and error code); no saved examples; collection variables baseUrl, token, userId, userEmail, userUsername, userPassword, mailToken; collection-level Bearer token (the token collection variable) inherited by protected requests, No Auth elsewhere; test scripts on Create/Login/Mail-create fill the variables; Create uses a collision-resistant qa_<suffix> email/username; optional query/header parameters start disabled. baseUrl is set from the Host and X-Forwarded-Proto of THIS request, so the file works for the deployment it was downloaded from. Pass ?download=false to view inline.

post.description: Teaching login for /store. Five personas share the password "secret_sauce": standard_user (everything works), locked_out_user (403 USER_LOCKED_OUT), problem_user (visual defects in the catalog: broken images, shifted names, one wrong price), performance_glitch_user (this request is answered after a 3 s server-side delay, then the catalog shows a 2.5 s loader), flaky_user ("Add to cart" fails on every odd attempt). An unknown username and a wrong password return the SAME 401 message, and the lock is checked only after the password matched, so the response never reveals whether a username exists. The returned session is NOT a token — nothing validates it; behavior is the source of truth the /store page applies. Rate limit: on average 30 attempts per minute per IP with a burst of 10 (token bucket, not a hard per-minute cap). Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

post.description: Mints an account with `metadata.role = "admin"`. Escalation happens only through this privileged path, which is the honest lesson. The seed code is published in the UI so every student gets their OWN admin; what keeps that safe is the data boundary, not the credential — admin mutations under /admin/* are scoped to your own account.

get.description: Returns one page of users plus exact total metadata. No authentication required. Defaults apply only when a parameter is ABSENT: a present-but-empty value (?sort=, ?filter=, ?search=, ?limit=) is rejected with 400. Validation order (first error wins): page → limit → per_page → sort → filter → search. Pagination: page 1-1000000; limit 1-100 (values above 100 are clamped to 100, per_page is a legacy alias — limit wins when both are given); a page beyond the last one returns 200 with an empty users array (no error). Sorting: sort=field[:asc|desc], default created_at:desc; sortable fields: created_at, updated_at, login_count, last_login_at, username, email. Non-unique fields get an _id tie-breaker in the same direction, so the order is deterministic for unchanged data (equal values never swap between pages); string sorting is binary (byte order, uppercase before lowercase); last_login_at may be null — nulls sort first ascending. Filtering: filter=field:value, repeatable; different fields are ANDed, the same field twice is rejected (DUPLICATE_FILTER_FIELD), max 10 filters; filterable fields: role (user|admin|moderator), is_active, is_verified, is_premium (strictly true|false), employment.status (employed|unemployed|student|retired|freelancer), settings.theme (light|dark|system), settings.language (2 lowercase letters), address.country (exact match, 1-64 characters). Only whitelisted fields and typed values ever reach the database — the input cannot inject query operators. Search: search=<1-64 characters>, case-insensitive substring over username, email, profile.first_name and profile.last_name; regex metacharacters are escaped (search=.* matches literal ".*"); combined with filters by AND; not index-backed. Response headers: X-Total-Count (exact number of matches before pagination — the same value as total in the body) and Link (RFC 8288: rel="first", "prev", "next", "last"; prev/next only when they exist; every link keeps your sort/filter/search parameters and canonicalises per_page to limit). total is exact (CountDocuments) but a best-effort snapshot: the count and the page are two operations, so concurrent creates or TTL deletes may shift them slightly.

get.description: Accepts GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE and stores whatever arrives — method, headers, query and body — then answers 202. This is the URL you paste into another system. If you send `X-PlayQA-Signature` in the Stripe-compatible form `t=<unix>,v1=<hex-hmac-sha256>` computed over `"<t>.<raw body>"` with the inbox signing secret, the stored event records whether it verified: `signature_valid` is `true`, `false`, or `null` when no signature header was sent at all. An event is stored either way — an invalid signature is never a reason to hide what arrived. The body is capped at 64 KiB. OPTIONS is answered by CORS and is not captured; browsers cannot send custom headers here, so call it server-to-server.

post.description: Creates an inbox that captures any HTTP request sent to its ingest URL — the HTTP counterpart of a temporary mailbox. Returns TWO tokens: `ingest_token` is public and appears in `ingest_url` (give it to the system that will call you), `token` is private and reads the captured events. `signing_secret` is returned ONCE, here: it is never repeated by GET /webhooks/{token}. The inbox and its events are deleted after 2 hours.

201.description: Inbox created; signing_secret is shown only in this response

429.description: Too many active inboxes for this address

get.description: Returns the inbox behind a private token, including its `ingest_url`, so a page that only stored the token can restore its session after a reload. The `signing_secret` is NOT returned here — it is shown once, when the inbox is created.

200.description: Inbox metadata without the signing secret

delete.description: Deletes the inbox and every event it captured. Idempotent for the caller's purposes: an already-deleted or expired token answers 404.

get.description: Returns captured events newest first — the async assertion target: poll it after triggering whatever sends the webhook. Bodies are represented by a 200-byte preview; fetch a single event for the full body and all headers. `dropped_count` is how many events were evicted because the inbox reached its cap of 100.

Returns the complete event: every captured header, the query, and the body. `body_encoding` is `utf8` for text and `base64` for anything that is not valid UTF-8 — a webhook body is whatever the caller sent, and binary payloads cannot live in a JSON string unencoded. Sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) are stored masked as `***`: that the request carried one is worth seeing, its value is not kept.
get.summary: Get one captured event in full

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and returns every text or binary frame unchanged.
The server sends a welcome frame first, pings every 30s, and closes with
1000 `session_timeout` after 10 minutes. Not callable from Swagger UI —
use `wscat -c wss://play-qa.com/api/v1/ws/echo` or any WebSocket client.

A request that is not a handshake answers 426 with `Connection: Upgrade`
and `Upgrade: websocket` (RFC 9110 §15.5.22 and §7.8). Both fields are
connection-specific and are not end-to-end guarantees: an intermediary
removes or reconstructs them for each hop. HTTP/2 forbids both fields
(RFC 9113 §8.2.2). On play-qa.com the origin pair is not visible —
identify the refusal by the 426 status, the `UPGRADE_REQUIRED` JSON code
and `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13`, which travels end to end.

has_active_token.description:
HasActiveToken reports whether access_token is non-empty, i.e. whether
the account is currently logged in. The token itself is never included:
an admin list that leaked bearer tokens would be account takeover.

seed_code.description:
SeedCode is compared in constant time against ADMIN_SEED_CODE. Bounded
before any comparison so an anonymous caller cannot make the server hash
an arbitrarily long string.

Deliberately NOT `required`. With it, Gin rejects an absent field at bind
time with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR while a WRONG code answers 403 — and that
difference is an oracle: it tells a caller whether the field was read at
all. Absent and wrong must be the same answer, so the empty string falls
through to the constant-time comparison and fails there like any other
wrong value. Measured: with `required` the two cases were 400 and 403.

dropped_count.description:
DroppedCount surfaces the trim so the UI can say "showing the last 100 of
137" rather than pretending nothing was evicted.

expires_at.description:
No omitempty on either: the contract is that the key is ALWAYS present
and carries null when the claim is absent or is not a number. A vanishing
key forces every client to tell "no exp" apart from "old server", which is
exactly the ambiguity the three-state signature_valid avoids.

headers.description:
Headers and Query keep REPEATED values: HTTP allows duplicate names, and a
map[string]string silently kept only the last one — a lossy capture in a
tool whose entire purpose is showing exactly what arrived (§3.4).

signature_valid.description:
SignatureValid has THREE states and nil is not false: nil means no signature
header was sent at all. The inbox always has a secret, so "nothing to check
with" is unreachable here — unlike /jwt/decode, whose null means the server
has no key. The UI must not borrow that wording (§2.1).

Bearer on POST /bug-reports is optional.
tags.name: Buggy

tags.description: Feature 11 — multipart upload and binary download. The media type is detected from the content (a valid extension with the wrong bytes is a 422), the filename is sanitised and returned in both Content-Disposition forms, and files live 24h. Bearer on upload and delete is optional: without it the file is anonymous and reachable only by its id; with it the file also appears in GET /files.
tags.name: Files

tags.description: Feature 12 — a SECOND, parallel authentication scheme: HS256 access and refresh tokens that live beside the opaque token and never replace it. Inspectable claims, a short access lifetime, a refresh flow, and a distinct error code for every reason a token can be refused (missing, malformed, forged, expired, wrong claims, wrong type). POST /jwt/decode reads any token without verifying it.
tags.name: JWT

tags.description: Server-Sent Events: one request the server keeps open and writes to as things happen. Read it with EventSource in a browser or `curl -N` on the command line. No authentication, no persistence.
tags.name: Streaming

tags.description: Feature 16 — a disposable inbox with a public URL that captures whatever is sent to it: method, headers, query and raw body, read back through a private token. TWO tokens, two capabilities: the ingest token appears in the URL handed to a sender and only writes, the private token only reads and deletes. Every business method is captured and all of them answer 202, including a request whose X-PlayQA-Signature does not verify — the verdict is reported in signature_valid (true, false, or null when nothing was signed), never in the status code. The signing secret is returned once, by the creation call. An inbox and its events live 2h, at most 100 events are kept, and each body is capped at 64 KiB.
tags.name: Webhooks

tags.description: Feature 17 — role-based access. Every account is `user` or `admin`; `metadata.role` always existed but granted nothing until now. The point of the namespace is the difference between 401 and 403: a missing or bad token is 401 (the credential was not accepted), while a valid non-admin token is 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED (it was accepted, and it is not enough). The same split now applies to the ordinary write routes — a valid token on someone else's `:id` answers 403 FORBIDDEN instead of the 401 it used to. Obtain an admin with POST /users/create-admin and the published seed code; admin mutations here are scoped to your own account, so one student cannot delete another's work.
tags.name: Admin
